$t^{5+5+5}=t^{15}$

$t^{15}$

$3\times4\timese^{7}\timese^{2}\timesf\timesf$

$12\timese^{7+2}\timesf^{1+1}=12\timese^{9}\timesf^{2}$

$12e^{9}f^{2}$

**[B1 B1]**

> 
> **B1**: For correct final expression (e.g. $12f^{2}e^{9}$ will also secure the mark).
> 
> Workings are not necessary for this question to secure either mark.

parts.problem_md:
Given that  $\frac{y^{5}\timesy^{n}}{y^{7}}=y^{12}$

work out the value of $n$
parts.solution_md:
> *Multiply both sides by *$y^{7}$

$y^{5}\timesy^{n}=y^{12}\timesy^{7}$

> *Simplify using laws of indices that state that to multiply indices with the same base, add their powers*

$y^{5+n}=y^{19}$

> *The base on each side is the same, therefore the powers must be equal*

$5+n=19$

**[M1 M1]**

> *Subtract 5 from each side*

$n=14$

$n=14$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1: **For one correct application of an index rule in powers of $y$ or for the correct equation in $n$.
> 
> **A1: **For a correct answer. $y^{14}$ is allowed.
